chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Sulayman, nephew of Hassan al-'Ijli, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'God did not create any permissible thing nor any forbidden thing except that it has limits — like the limits of this house of mine. Whatever was from the road is from the road, and whatever was from the house is from the house, even down to the compensation for a scratch and whatever is beyond that, and the lashing and half of the lashing.'

key_terms.أَرْش: Arsh — the monetary compensation (blood money) prescribed for a physical injury that does not result in death; here used for even the smallest injury (a scratch)
key_terms.الْجَلْدَة: A single lash/stroke; the unit of corporal punishment in Islamic legal penalties
key_terms.حَرَام: Haram — that which is divinely forbidden
key_terms.حَلَال: Halal — that which is divinely permitted
key_terms.حُدُود: Legal limits or boundaries (hudud); in Islamic law, refers both to divinely mandated penalties and the boundaries demarcating the permissible from the forbidden

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the limits of halal and haram in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the vivid analogy of a house with a road running alongside it to illustrate that every legal ruling in Islamic law — whether permissible or forbidden — has precisely defined boundaries. Just as physical property has clear demarcations, divine law has precise limits that govern every matter, no matter how minor, extending even to the exact compensation for the smallest injury (a scratch) and the precise number of lashes in a legal penalty. This teaching emphasizes that Islamic jurisprudence is comprehensive and systematic, leaving no aspect of life — however small — without a defined ruling.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Aban Bin Usman, from Suleyman cousin of Hassan Al Ajaly who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not Create a Permissible nor a Prohibition except for it is a Limit like the limits (boundaries) of this house of mine<sup>asws</sup>. Whatever was from the road, so it is from the road, and whatever was from the house, so it is from the house, to the extent of the compensation of the scratch, and whatever is besides it, and the lashing and half of the lashing’.
